title: U.S. House · Wisconsin's 4th Congressional District
area: The city of Milwaukee and near suburbs.

context.text: Incumbent Gwen Moore (D) defeated Amy Donahue 70.5%-29.3% in the Democratic primary. Tim Rogers advanced from the Republican primary. Arthur Burks also qualified as an independent for the general-election ballot; two other independents, Carlos Dixon and Robert Raymond, withdrew or were disqualified.

candidates.name: Gwen Moore
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Amy Donahue 70.5%-29.3% in the Democratic primary.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 4th Congressional District (since 2005)

positions.summary: In a 2026 statement on ICE arrests in Milwaukee she said ICE is operating like a rogue agency and that serious reforms are long overdue.
positions.quote: ICE is operating like a rogue agency, and its abuses make clear that serious reforms are long overdue.

positions.summary: In a 2026 release introducing the Keep Public Funds in Public Schools Act, she criticized the federal tax-credit voucher program and state voucher funding.
positions.quote: Instead of investing in our public schools, which educate most of America’s students, Republicans used taxpayer funds to create a national voucher scheme.

positions.summary: In a 2026 statement she called legislation including the SAVE America Act voter suppression.
positions.quote: I continue to be disappointed that Rep. Steil, who represents my birthplace of Racine, is the architect of such voter suppression legislation, like the Voter ID Act and the so-called SAVE America Act.

record.text: Serves on the Joint Economic Committee and the House Committee on Ways and Means (Social Security, Tax, and Work and Welfare subcommittees) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.researchNotes: Her official website lists issue areas (economy and jobs, health care, immigration, environment, veterans, among others) but no extractable position statements were found as of the research date.

candidates.name: Tim Rogers

priorities.text: Lists universal school choice as an issue, saying school choice and voucher programs let students reach their full potential.
priorities.quote: I support School Choice and School Voucher programs.

priorities.text: Says one of his first priorities is a clean water emergency declaration for areas with crumbling infrastructure.
priorities.quote: One of my first priorities is to declare a clean water emergency for the areas of our country that need it the most.

priorities.text: Lists lowering taxes and reducing government spending.
priorities.quote: I, Tim Rogers, want to let taxpayers keep more of their money.

positions.summary: Campaign issues page says he supports school choice and school voucher programs.
positions.quote: I support School Choice and School Voucher programs.

candidates.researchNotes: Rogers has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. Statements come from the issues page of his campaign website; the page is not dated and matches the text Ballotpedia quoted from his 2022 and 2024 sites.

statements.quote: If elected, I will work to destroy the progressive tax system.

candidates.name: Arthur Burks

priorities.text: Platform lists livable wages, local business investment and vocational training.
priorities.quote: We advocate for livable wages, local business investment, and vocational training that prepares our youth for the high-demand jobs of tomorrow.

priorities.text: Platform lists protecting voting rights and prioritizing grassroots representation over party politics.
priorities.quote: Arthur is committed to protecting voting rights and ending the gridlock in Washington by prioritizing grassroots representation over party machine politics.

candidates.researchNotes: Has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 survey. Statements come from his campaign platform page, which is written in the third person.

statements.quote: Burks supports comprehensive gun safety legislation and funding for violence interruption programs that address crime at its roots.
statements.context: On his campaign platform page (written in the third person)
